one_liner: Datadog has a broad REST API with self-serve API/app keys and PATs; OAuth is partner-only; an official remote MCP server exists; builder access is via a 14-day free trial.
auth_notes: Users generate an API key + application key, or newer Personal Access Tokens. Datadog's docs say OAuth is only for approved Technology Partners and standalone OAuth clients are not supported, so OAUTH2 is not counted for a third-party developer. Composio's catalog lists OAUTH2 (and the MCP uses its own OAuth), but the pages do not show a self-serve OAuth app registration for the main API.
access_notes: Datadog's blog says new users can sign up for a free 14-day trial. The pages do not mention a permanent free tier. Keys are created inside a Datadog org.
blocker_notes: Builder access is via a short 14-day trial. Multi-user OAuth is limited to approved partners, so the toolkit must use per-customer API/app keys or PATs.

evidence.quote: Requests that write data require reporting access and require an `API key`. Requests that read data require full access and also require an `application key`.
Unlike application keys, PATs do not need to be paired with an API key.
OAuth is available only to approved Technology Partners developing official Datadog integrations. Standalone OAuth clients are not supported.
